1.why: All /api/mfa/* handlers derive the account exclusively from session.accountId of the authenticated session cookie; no client-supplied user identifier is accepted, so only the owner can view or modify their MFA record.

2.why: Each identity code is stored per preAuth session and compared via timingSafeEqual against pending.identityCode tied to the __Host-preauth cookie and account, so a code issued for one sign-in does not work for any other user.

3.why: The /api/mfa/confirm handler sets record.active=true but never deletes or rotates entries in the sessions map, so any previously issued sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled (statement is literally true, though a weakness).

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM-256 encrypted (encryptSecret) and recovery codes are stored as HMAC-SHA-256 hashes with a pepper (recoveryHash); plaintext is never persisted.

5.why: All tokens, the six-digit identity code, the TOTP secret, recovery codes, the pepper, and the AES key are generated with crypto.getRandomValues or crypto.subtle, i.e., a CSPRNG.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB is used anywhere in the client; the session and pre-auth cookies are HttpOnly, and the CSRF token and setup secret are held only in JS memory/DOM.

7.why: Server-side validators validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, and normaliseRecovery strictly regex-check all user input, and apiBody enforces a plain JSON object before use.

8.why: All dynamic values (secret, URI, codes, messages) are rendered via textContent; the only innerHTML assignments use fixed static strings, and a nonce-based CSP blocks injected inline script.

9.why: The server issues no redirects at all (no Location headers or redirect parameters); navigation is fixed internal SPA views and hard-coded /api paths, so no open redirect is possible.

10.why: securityHeaders sets a nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, plus Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy on every response.

11.why: secureCookie sets __Host-session and __Host-preauth with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict (and Path=/ with the __Host- prefix).

12.why: In the default TEST_MODE the mock identity code and all recovery codes are written to the visible Logs panel and browser console (log('TEST ONLY — ...')), so codes are not kept out of logs, although errors are generic with no stack traces.

13.why: Identity codes expire after 10 minutes (PREAUTH_TIMEOUT_MS) and are marked used/deleted on success; recovery codes are marked used in recoveryCodes; TOTP setup counters are tracked in usedSetupCounters to block reuse.

14.why: failAttempt increments counters and imposes a 10-minute lock after 5 failures (MAX_FAILURES/LOCK_MS), enforced via locked() checks returning 429 on identity verify, MFA confirm, and recovery endpoints.

15.why: A fresh random session token is issued at authentication with the pre-auth cookie expired, sessions enforce 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
